docs.title: EurocodePy
docs.text:
EurocodePy is a Python library for structural design calculations according to the Eurocode standards. It provides composable, engineering-focused building blocks — reusable calculations, material databases, load combinations, and section utilities — that you can drop into your own scripts and notebooks.

Source code: https://github.com/pcachim/eurocodepy — the version is the one of pyproject.toml

docs.title: Material databases
docs.text:
Material characteristic and design values are stored in a bundled database and exposed through typed Python classes. Supported materials:

Material Grades / Types Concrete C12/15 to C100/115 (EN 1992-1-1:2004 and 2023) Reinforcement B400A/B/C, B500A/B/C, B600–B700, A400NR, A500NR, A500EL Prestressing steel Y1770, Y1860, and others Structural steel S235, S275, S355, S450 Timber Softwood (C), Hardwood (D), Glulam (GL), CLT, LVL Bolts Grades 4.6 through 10.9

docs.title: Steel section profiles
docs.text:
European hot-rolled profiles are available as named enumerations and dataclasses:

  • I-profiles: IPE, HEA, HEB, HEM
  • Hollow sections: CHS (circular), RHS (rectangular), SHS (square)

docs.title: Eurocode modules
docs.text: Module Standard Coverage ec1 EN 1991 Load combinations (ULS, SLS, ALS), wind, snow, load types ec2 EN 1992 Concrete materials (2004 and 2023), ULS beam/shear/torsion/shell/slab/punching, detailing, Annex B creep and shrinkage, SLS crack, fire ec3 EN 1993 Steel materials, profiles, bolted and welded connections, ULS checks ec5 EN 1995 Timber materials, ULS bending/shear, SLS vibration/deformation ec7 EN 1997 Bearing resistance, earth pressures, soil materials ec8 EN 1998 Design response spectra, national annex parameters utils — Section properties, principal stresses, stress invariants

docs.title: Editions and National Annex support
docs.text: Functions take edition= (2004 or 2023) and annex= (country code). Portuguese data (seismic and wind zones, live loads) is bundled and further annexes are registered with register_annex; see Editions and National Annexes.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import eurocodepy as ec

# --- Concrete material (EN 1992) ---
concrete = ec.Concrete('C30/37')
print(concrete.fck)   # characteristic compressive strength [MPa]
print(concrete.fcd)   # design compressive strength [MPa]

# --- Steel material (EN 1993) ---
steel = ec.Steel('S355')
print(steel.fyk)   # yield strength [MPa]

# --- Timber material (EN 1995) ---
timber = ec.Timber('C24')
print(timber.fmk)  # characteristic bending strength [MPa]

# --- Design response spectrum (EN 1998, Portuguese NA) ---
spec = ec.spectrum.get_spectrum_ec8(
    locale='PT', code='PT1', imp_class='II',
    soil='C', zone='1_2', behaviour=3.0
)
ec.spectrum.draw_spectrum_ec8(spec, show=False)   # show=True opens the window

# --- Load combinations (EN 1990) ---
from eurocodepy.ec1 import Load, LoadType, Loads
loads = Loads()
loads.add(Load('G1', LoadType.PERMANENT, 1.0, 1.35, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0))   # γ fav, γ unf, ψ0, ψ1, ψ2
loads.add(Load('Q1', LoadType.LIVE, 0.0, 1.5, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3))
loads.add(Load('W1', LoadType.WIND, 0.0, 1.5, 0.6, 0.2, 0.0))
uls = loads.get_ULS_combos()

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# From PyPI
pip install eurocodepy

# With uv
uv add eurocodepy

# Latest development version from GitHub
pip install git+https://github.com/pcachim/eurocodepy.git

Requires Python ≥ 3.12.

docs.title: Python Style Guide
docs.text: This document outlines the guidelines for writing Python code for our project. Following these guidelines helps ensure that the code is consistent and easy to read.

docs.title: Code Formatting
docs.text:
• Use 4 spaces for indentation.
  • Use a space after the # for inline comments.
  • Use blank lines to separate logical sections of code.
if x > 0:
    print('x is positive')
else:
    print('x is non-positive')

# This is an inline comment.

def function_name(parameter):
    # Code inside function.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
• Use descriptive names that accurately reflect the purpose of the variable.
  • Use snake_case for variable names.
number_of_items = 5
total_price = 10.50

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
• Use descriptive names that accurately reflect the purpose of the function.
  • Use snake_case for function names.
def calculate_total_price(quantity, price):
    return quantity * price
````

### Classes

- Use PascalCase for class names.

```python
class User:
    # ...
````

### File Names

- Use snake_case for file names.

```text
main_script.py
user_profile.py

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
• Use comments to explain non-obvious or complex code.
  • Use complete sentences and proper grammar.
  • Begin comments with a capital letter.
  • Use one space after the # for inline comments.
  • Use multi-line comments for longer explanations.
# Add the value to the list.
my_list.append(value)

"""
This function takes two parameters:
- name: a string representing the name of the user
- age: an integer representing the age of the user

It returns a greeting message.
"""

    # ...

docs.text:
• Use double quotes for strings.
  • Use parentheses for tuple packing and unpacking.
  • Always use is or is not to compare with None.
  • Use a blank line before and after a return statement.
  • Use None instead of '' or [] for default values of function arguments.

```python message = "Hello, world!" print(message)

a, b, c = (1, 2, 3)

if x is None: # ...

def my_function(arg1, arg2=None): # ...

def my_other_function(arg1, arg2=[]): # This is bad.

def my_good_function(arg1, arg2=None): if arg2 is None: arg2 = [] # ... ````

docs.title: Background & Design Philosophy
docs.text: This section explains the why behind EurocodePy — its goals, design decisions, and how the pieces fit together. Read this if you want to understand the library deeply rather than just use it.

docs.title: Why EurocodePy was created
docs.text:
Structural engineers working in Python face a recurring problem: Eurocode calculations are well-defined in the standards, but translating them into reliable, readable code is repetitive and error-prone. Each project reinvents the same material property look-ups, the same load combination logic, the same unit conversions.

EurocodePy aims to provide the missing layer of shared building blocks — small, composable functions and classes that can be dropped into any project, notebook, or parametric model without pulling in a large framework.

The design philosophy is:

  • Pragmatic over complete. Not every clause of every part needs to be implemented. What matters is that the implemented parts are correct, well-tested, and easy to use.
  • Transparent. Formulas follow the code clauses directly. Variable names mirror the standard notation (e.g. fck, fyd, VRd_c) so it is straightforward to trace a computation back to its source equation.
  • Composable. Each module is independently useful. You can use ec2 alone without importing ec7, or mix ec1 load combinations with a custom section analysis.

docs.title: Architecture overview
docs.text:
eurocodepy/
├── dbase       ← JSON-backed material & section database; editions (`Editions`) and annex-aware lookups
├── annex       ← National Annexes: one JSON per country (data/national_annexes), `register_annex`
├── units       ← Unit system abstractions (SI, kN/mm, N/mm)
├── calc_report ← `CalcReport`: the steps of a check (`trace=`), as dict, JSON or Markdown
├── national_parameters  ← Portuguese municipal data (seismic, wind, snow, temperature)
├── ec1         ← EN 1991: load types, forces, combinations (ULS/SLS/ALS), wind
├── ec2         ← EN 1992: concrete, reinforcement, prestress; ULS and SLS of 2004 (uls, sls)
│                  and of 2023 (uls2023, time_dependent2023); slabs, membranes and shells
├── ec3         ← EN 1993: steel materials, profiles, connections, classification, section and member checks
├── ec5         ← EN 1995: timber materials, ULS checks (2004 and 2025), SLS vibration
├── ec7         ← EN 1997: soils, bearing resistance, earth pressures
├── ec8         ← EN 1998: response spectra, national annex parameters
└── utils       ← Cross sections, section properties, stress calculations

Each Eurocode module follows a consistent internal layout where it makes sense:

ecN/
├── __init__.py   ← public exports
├── materials.py  ← material classes and grade enumerations
├── uls/          ← Ultimate Limit State check functions (edition 2004)
├── uls2023/      ← the same for the second generation where it changed (ec2; ec5 has uls2025)
└── sls/          ← Serviceability Limit State check functions

The functions of the second generation mirror the old ones (ec2.uls / ec2.uls2023), so a check can be swapped by changing the import or the edition= argument.

docs.title: Material database
docs.text:
Material properties are stored in a JSON file bundled with the package. The dbase module loads this file at import time and exposes the data through typed pandas DataFrames and Python dataclasses. This approach means:

  • Properties are easy to inspect and update without changing code.
  • The same data is accessible both via the high-level material classes (e.g. Concrete('C30/37')) and directly via dbase.db for custom queries.

docs.title: Unit systems
docs.text:
Structural engineering practice uses several different unit systems. The units module provides three pre-defined UnitSystem objects:

Name Force Length Pressure SI N m Pa kN_mm kN mm kN/mm² = GPa N_mm N mm N/mm² = MPa

Functions throughout the library accept numeric inputs; the caller is responsible for passing values in a consistent unit system. The UnitSystem objects are provided as a reference — they are not yet used to automatically convert inputs.

docs.title: Load combinations (EC1)
docs.text:
The ec1.combos module implements EN 1990 load combination logic using Python dataclasses and enumerations. A LoadCombinations object takes a list of Load objects (each tagged with a LoadType) and generates all required combinations for the requested limit state (CombinationType.ULS, SLS_K, SLS_FR, SLS_QP, ALS, or FLS).

The combination factors (ψ₀, ψ₁, ψ₂) are looked up from a built-in table keyed on LoadType. Custom ψ values are not yet supported.

docs.title: Seismic spectra (EC8)
docs.text:
The ec8.spectrum module supports both the standard Eurocode horizontal spectrum and the Portuguese National Annex (two continental zones and Azores). Spectra are returned as dictionaries of period–acceleration pairs that can be plotted with draw_spectrum_ec8 or exported to CSV with write_spectrum_ec8.

Key parameters follow the standard notation: ag (reference peak ground acceleration), S (soil factor), T_B, T_C, T_D (corner periods). The behaviour factor q is applied when generating a design (inelastic) spectrum.

docs.title: Status and roadmap
docs.text:
EurocodePy is early-stage. The APIs are functional but may change between releases as the library matures. Contributions are welcome — see CONTRIBUTING_GUIDELINES.md for how to get involved.

Areas actively being developed:

  • EN 1992-1-1:2023 (second generation Eurocode 2): concrete done (materials, shear, torsion, detailing, Annex B and G); columns, crack width and anchorage still 2004
  • Second-generation code for EC3 and for the rest of EC2 (columns, crack width, anchorage)
  • EN 1995 connection design and snow loads (EN 1991-1-3)
  • National annexes: the Portuguese NDPs of EN 1992-1-1:2023, and other countries

docs.title: How-to Guides
docs.text: Practical recipes for common tasks. Unlike tutorials, each guide assumes you already have EurocodePy installed and focuses on getting one specific thing done.

docs.title: How to look up a material
docs.text:
import eurocodepy as ec

# Concrete — access all grades via the enum
concrete = ec.Concrete('C25/30')
print(concrete.fck, concrete.fcd, concrete.Ecm)

# Steel
steel = ec.Steel('S275')
print(steel.fyk, steel.fuk)

# Timber
timber = ec.Timber('GL28h')
print(timber.fmk, timber.E0mean)

Alternatively browse the raw database:

# List all available concrete grades
print(list(ec.ConcreteGrades))

# List all reinforcement grades
print(list(ec.ReinforcementGrades))

# List all timber grades
print(list(ec.TimberGrades))

docs.title: How to access Portuguese national annex parameters
docs.text:
from eurocodepy import NationalParams, get_national_params, seismic_get_params, wind_get_params

# Data of a municipality (seismic zones, accelerations, snow and wind zones, temperatures)
data = get_national_params(concelho='Coimbra')
print(data['ZonaSismica1'], data['Acel1'], data['ZonaVento'])

# Spectrum parameters of the Portuguese NA: code, type, soil, importance class
seismic = seismic_get_params('PT', 'PT1', 'C', 'ii')
print(seismic)           # S_max, S_min, a_g1, a_g2, T_B, T_C, T_D, ImportanceCoef

# Wind: vb,0, z_min, z_0 and z_0,II of a zone and terrain category
vb0, z_min, z0, z0_ii = wind_get_params('PT', 'ZonaA', 'II')

# NationalParams holds the locale and the municipality (default: Lisboa)
params = NationalParams(concelho='Braga')
print(params.local, params.concelho)

docs.title: How to define a unit system
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.units import SI, kN_mm, N_mm, UnitType

# Each system gives the SI value of its units
print(SI.force, SI.distance, SI.pressure)              # N, m, Pa
print(kN_mm.force, kN_mm.distance, kN_mm.pressure)     # kN, mm, kN/mm²
print(N_mm.force, N_mm.distance, N_mm.pressure)        # N, mm, N/mm²

# Factor that converts a value from one system to another
f = SI.convert_to(kN_mm, UnitType.FORCE)               # newtons -> kilonewtons: 0.001

docs.title: How to build load combinations
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec1 import Load, LoadType, Loads

loads = Loads()
#                  name  type                 γ fav  γ unf  ψ0   ψ1   ψ2
loads.add(Load("G", LoadType.PERMANENT, 1.0, 1.35, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
loads.add(Load("Q", LoadType.LIVE,      0.0, 1.50, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3))
loads.add(Load("W", LoadType.WIND,      0.0, 1.50, 0.6, 0.2, 0.0))

values = {"G": 20.0, "Q": 8.0, "W": 4.0}                 # characteristic values [kN/m²]

# ULS (EN 1990 Eq. 6.10): a dict {name: LoadCombination}; factors = {load name: (Load, factor)}
for name, combo in loads.get_ULS_combos().items():
    total = sum(factor * values[k] for k, (_, factor) in combo.factors.items())
    print(f"{name:34s} {total:7.2f}")

# SLS characteristic, frequent and quasi-permanent
for name, combo in loads.get_SLS_combos().items():
    print(name)

docs.title: How to calculate creep and shrinkage (EN 1992-1-1:2023, Annex B)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2.sls.creep import creep_coef
from eurocodepy.ec2.sls.shrinkage import shrink_strain

# C30/37: fcm,28 = 38 MPa; RH = 60 %; hn = 2Ac/u = 200 mm; class CN
# Creep coefficient φ(t, t0): loaded at t0 = 28 days, t = 50 years
phi = creep_coef(t=18250 + 28, t0=28, fcm28=38.0, RH=60, hn=200, t0_T=28, concrete_class="CN")
print(f"φ = {phi:.2f}")

# Total shrinkage strain, drying from ts = 1 day (alpha_NDP_b = alpha_NDP_d = 1: recommended)
eps_cs = shrink_strain(t=18251, ts=1, fcm28=38.0, RH=60, hn=200, concrete_class="CN",
                       alpha_NDP_b=1.0, alpha_NDP_d=1.0)
print(f"εcs = {eps_cs:.6f}")

docs.title: How to follow the strain history of a concrete member (EN 1992-1-1:2023, Annex B)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2 import time_dependent2023 as td

fcm, ecm = 38.0, 33000.0          # C30/37: fcm,28 and Ecm,28 [MPa]
common = dict(fcm28=fcm, ecm28=ecm, rh=60.0, hn=200.0, cls="CN")

# Compressive stress of 10 MPa applied at 28 days, 5 MPa more at 90 days: stress-dependent strain at 50 years
eps = td.strain_history(18278, [(28, -10.0), (90, -5.0)], **common)

# Compliance J(t, t0) and the shrinkage at the same age
j = td.creep_compliance(18278, 28, **common)                  # 1/MPa
eps_cs = td.shrinkage_total(18278, 1, fcm, rh=60.0, hn=200.0, cls="CN")

docs.title: How to use the partial factors of another design situation (EN 1992-1-1:2023, Table 4.3)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2 import Concrete, material_partial_factors

material_partial_factors("2023", "accidental")                 # γs, γc, γce, γv of the situation
accidental = Concrete("C30/37", edition="2023", situation="accidental")
print(accidental.gamma_c, accidental.fcd)

The check inputs (PunchInput, ShearInput, MembraneInput, …) have from_partial_factors(edition, situation, ...).

docs.title: How to produce a calculation report
docs.text:
Most checks accept trace= with a CalcReport: each step (symbol, value, unit, clause, expression) is recorded and the report can be written as a dictionary, JSON or Markdown with LaTeX.

from eurocodepy.calc_report import CalcReport
from eurocodepy.ec2.uls import design_anchorage_length

report = CalcReport(title="Anchorage of a ϕ16 bar")
anchorage = design_anchorage_length(phi=16, fck=30, fyk=500, cd=40, good_bond=True, trace=report)

print(report.to_markdown())          # sections with the clause and the formula of each step
data = report.to_dict()              # {'schema_version', 'title', 'meta', 'sections': [...]}

The checks of EC2 (uls, uls2023), EC3 (section_check_profile, member_check_profile, classify_section) and EC5 take it; with trace=None (the default) nothing is recorded.

docs.title: How to check shear resistance of a concrete beam (EN 1992)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2.uls.shear import calc_vrdc, calc_vrd, calc_vrdmax, calc_asws

# Section and material
b_w = 0.30   # web width [m]
d   = 0.46   # effective depth [m]
rho = 0.0117 # tensile reinforcement ratio As/(b_w·d)
fck, g_c = 30, 1.5     # [MPa]
fyk, g_s = 500, 1.15   # shear reinforcement [MPa]

# Design shear resistance without shear reinforcement [kN]
vrd_min, vrd_c, vrd = calc_vrdc(b_w, d, fck, g_c, rho)
print(f"VRd,c = {vrd:.1f} kN")

# Required shear reinforcement for VEd = 180 kN, cot θ = 2
asw_s, vrd_max = calc_asws(b_w, d, fck, g_c, fyk, g_s, 2.0, 180.0)
print(f"Asw/s = {asw_s * 1e4:.2f} cm²/m (VRd,max = {vrd_max:.0f} kN)")

docs.title: How to compute earth pressures (EN 1997)
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from eurocodepy.ec7 import pressure_coefficients, EarthPressureModels

phi   = np.radians(30.0)   # soil friction angle
delta = np.radians(15.0)   # wall friction angle
theta = 0.0                # slope of the backfill
beta  = 0.0                # slope of the wall

# Ka, Kp, Kaq, Kpq, dkas1, dkps1, dkas2, dkps2
Ka, Kp, *_ = pressure_coefficients(phi, delta, theta, beta, method=EarthPressureModels.COULOMB)
print(f"Ka = {Ka:.3f},  Kp = {Kp:.3f}")

docs.title: How to plot and export a seismic spectrum
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec8.spectrum import get_spectrum_ec8, draw_spectrum_ec8, write_spectrum_ec8

spec = get_spectrum_ec8(
    locale='EU', code='CEN_1',
    imp_class='II', soil='B',
    zone='.3g', behaviour=4.0,
)

# Display the plot interactively
draw_spectrum_ec8(spec, show=False)   # show=True opens the window

# Save a CSV for import into SAP2000, ETABS, etc.
write_spectrum_ec8(spec, filename='spectrum_EU_CEN1_II_B_03g_q4.csv')

docs.title: How to calculate section properties
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.utils import RectangularCrossSection

section = RectangularCrossSection(0.30, 0.60)      # m
print(section.area, section.inertia_y, section.bend_mod_y)

For reinforced sections (cracked and uncracked properties) see utils.calc_section_rectangular in the utils module.

docs.title: How to use a National Annex
docs.text:
The values in eurocodes.json are the ones recommended by the Eurocodes. What a National Annex changes is a patch kept in its own file, data/national_annexes/<COUNTRY>.json (Portugal's is built in: its wind, seismic and live-load data). The functions that depend on Nationally Determined Parameters take annex= with the country code:

from eurocodepy.ec2 import Concrete, material_partial_factors
from eurocodepy.ec2.uls2023 import detailing

Concrete("C30/37", edition="2023", annex="PT")        # the annex's values, if it has any
material_partial_factors("2023", "persistent")         # annex=None: the Eurocode's values
detailing.beam_max_spacings(0.5, annex="PT")

An unknown code raises ValueError and lists the available ones. Add your own annex (a JSON file or a dict) with register_annex; it has the same shape as the Editions entries of eurocodes.json, so it patches one value of a table and leaves the rest as recommended:

import eurocodepy as ec

ec.register_annex({
    "country": "XX",
    "editions": {"ec2": {"2023": {
        "partial_factors": {"materials": {"persistent": {"gamma_c": 1.4}}},
        "detailing": {"beams": {"s_l_max": 0.7}},
    }}},
})
Concrete("C30/37", edition="2023", annex="XX").gamma_c    # 1.4
ec.available_annexes()                                      # ['PT', 'XX']

loads (wind, seismic, live) in the file add the country next to EU, so wind_get_params("XX", ...) and the EC1/EC7/EC8 functions find it. The package only ships the values it can source; it never invents an annex.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text: Step-by-step worked examples that take you from zero to a working calculation. Each tutorial is self-contained — copy, paste, and run.

docs.title: Tutorial 1 — Concrete beam bending check (EN 1992)
docs.text:
This tutorial shows how to define concrete and reinforcement materials, then check the bending resistance of a rectangular section.

import eurocodepy as ec

# 1. Define materials
concrete = ec.Concrete('C30/37')   # fck = 30 MPa
reinf    = ec.Reinforcement('B500B')  # fyk = 500 MPa

print(f"fck  = {concrete.fck} MPa")
print(f"fcd  = {concrete.fcd:.2f} MPa")   # design value (fck / γc)
print(f"fyk  = {reinf.fyk} MPa")
print(f"fyd  = {reinf.fyd:.2f} MPa")      # design value (fyk / γs)

# 2. Section geometry
b   = 300   # width [mm]
h   = 500   # total depth [mm]
c   = 30    # nominal cover [mm]
phi = 16    # bar diameter [mm]
n   = 4     # number of bars

d   = h - c - phi / 2   # effective depth [mm]
As  = n * 3.14159 * (phi / 2) ** 2   # reinforcement area [mm²]
print(f"d    = {d:.1f} mm")
print(f"As   = {As:.1f} mm²")

# 3. Calculate design bending resistance (simplified rectangular stress block)
Mrd, eps_s, x = ec.ec2.calc_mrd(b / 1000, d / 1000, As / 100, concrete.fcd, reinf.fyd)   # m, cm²
print(f"MRd  = {Mrd:.1f} kNm")

docs.title: 4. The same section with the second-generation code (EN 1992-1-1:2023)
docs.text: concrete23 = ec.ec2.get_concrete('C30/37', edition='2023') # fcd = η_cc·k_tc·fck/γc, Eq. 5.3 reinf23 = ec.ec2.Reinforcement('B500B', edition='2023') print(f"fcd (2023) = {concrete23.fcd:.2f} MPa, fyd (2023) = {reinf23.fyd:.2f} MPa") Mrd23, eps_s, x = ec.ec2.calc_mrd(b / 1000, d / 1000, As / 100, concrete23.fcd, reinf23.fyd) print(f"MRd (2023) = {Mrd23:.1f} kNm")

docs.title: For fck > 40 MPa the 2023 design strength is reduced by η_cc, and k_tc depends on the loading
docs.text:
c50 = ec.ec2.get_concrete('C50/60', edition='2023', loading='other') print(f"C50/60: η_cc = {c50.eta_cc:.3f}, k_tc = {c50.k_tc}, fcd = {c50.fcd:.2f} MPa")


---

## Tutorial 2 — Design response spectrum (EN 1998, Portuguese NA)

This tutorial generates and plots the horizontal elastic design spectrum for a
building in Lisbon using the Portuguese National Annex.

```python
import eurocodepy as ec

# Spectrum parameters
# locale   : 'PT'  — Portuguese national annex
# code     : 'PT1' — type 1 spectrum (continental Portugal)
# imp_class: 'II'   — importance class II (ordinary buildings)
# soil     : 'C'    — medium-dense soil (Vs,30 = 180–360 m/s)
# zone     : '1_2'  — seismic zone 1.2
# behaviour: 3.0    — behaviour factor q for ductile frame

spec = ec.spectrum.get_spectrum_ec8(
    locale='PT',
    code='PT1',
    imp_class='II',
    soil='C',
    zone='1_2',
    behaviour=3.0,
)

# Print a few values
print("ag   =", spec.attrs['a_g'], "m/s2")   # design ground acceleration
print("S    =", spec.attrs['S'])             # soil factor
print("peak =", spec['value'].max(), "m/s2") # largest ordinate of the design spectrum

# Plot (show=True opens the window)
ec.spectrum.draw_spectrum_ec8(spec, show=False)

# Export to CSV for use in structural analysis software
ec.spectrum.write_spectrum_ec8(spec, filename='spectrum_PT1_II_C_1_2.csv')

docs.title: Tutorial 3 — Load combinations (EN 1990)
docs.text:
This tutorial builds a set of ULS and SLS load combinations from individual loads.

from eurocodepy.ec1 import Load, LoadType, Loads

# Each load carries its partial factors (γ favourable and unfavourable) and ψ0, ψ1, ψ2
loads = Loads()
loads.add(Load("Self-weight", LoadType.PERMANENT, 1.0, 1.35, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
loads.add(Load("Live load",   LoadType.LIVE,      0.0, 1.50, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3))
loads.add(Load("Wind",        LoadType.WIND,      0.0, 1.50, 0.6, 0.2, 0.0))
loads.add(Load("Snow",        LoadType.SNOW,      0.0, 1.50, 0.5, 0.2, 0.0))

# ULS combinations (EN 1990 expression 6.10): {name: LoadCombination}
for name in loads.get_ULS_combos():
    print(name)

# SLS combinations: characteristic (SLS-K), frequent (SLS-FR) and quasi-permanent (SLS-QP)
for name, combo in loads.get_SLS_combos().items():
    if combo.type.value == "SLS-QP":
        print(name)

# Apply a combination to the values of the loads (here kN/m²)
values = {"Self-weight": 10.0, "Live load": 5.0, "Wind": 3.0, "Snow": 1.5}
combo = next(iter(loads.get_ULS_combos().values()))
print(sum(f * values[k] for k, (_, f) in combo.factors.items()))

docs.title: Tutorial 4 — Timber bending check (EN 1995)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec5.materials import SolidTimber, ServiceClass, LoadDuration

# Define timber grade
timber = SolidTimber('C24')

# Material properties
print(f"fm,k  = {timber.fmk} MPa")        # characteristic bending strength
print(f"E0,mean = {timber.E0mean} MPa")   # mean modulus of elasticity

# Modification factor for Service Class 1, Medium-term loading
kmod = timber.k_mod(
    service_class=ServiceClass.SC1,
    load_duration=LoadDuration.MediumDuration,
)
print(f"kmod  = {kmod}")

# Design bending strength
fm_d = kmod * timber.fmk / timber.safety     # γM = 1.3 for solid timber (Table 2.3 EN 1995)
print(f"fm,d  = {fm_d:.2f} MPa")

# The same, in one call
print(timber.design_values(ServiceClass.SC1, LoadDuration.MediumDuration)["fmd"])

docs.title: Tutorial 5 — Steel section and bearing capacity (EN 1993 / EN 1997)
docs.text:
import numpy as np
import eurocodepy as ec

# Steel section (catalogue units: cm, cm², cm⁴)
steel   = ec.Steel('S355')
profile = ec.ec3.ProfilesI['IPE300']

print(f"fy   = {steel.fyk} MPa")
print(f"A    = {profile.A} cm²")
print(f"Iy   = {profile.Iy:.0f} cm⁴")

# Section check under MEd = 100 kNm and VEd = 80 kN
check = ec.ec3.section_check_profile(
    profile, steel.fyk, ec.ec3.SectionForces(my_ed=100.0, vz_ed=80.0))
print(f"utilization = {check.utilization:.2f}")

# Shallow foundation bearing capacity (EN 1997): angles in radians
phi = np.radians(30.0)
R = ec.ec7.bearing_resistance(
    Bx=1.5, By=2.0, Hx=20.0, Hy=0.0, N=200.0,    # m, kN
    phi=phi, gamma=18.0, q=0.8 * 18.0, c=0.0,
)
print(f"Rd   = {R:.1f}")

docs.title: Tutorial 6 — Slab or shell with shear: sandwich model, 2004 and 2023
docs.text:
A 200 mm slab-shell with membrane forces, bending, torsion and out-of-plane shear is designed with the sandwich model of EN 1992-2 Annex LL (2004) and of EN 1992-1-1:2023, Annex G. Forces are per metre (kN/m, kNm/m), lengths in m and strengths in MPa.

from eurocodepy.ec2 import uls, uls2023

forces = dict(n_xx=100.0, n_yy=50.0, n_xy=20.0,         # membrane [kN/m]
              m_xx=20.0, m_yy=10.0, m_xy=5.0,           # bending and torsion [kNm/m]
              v_x=250.0, v_y=80.0)                      # out-of-plane shear [kN/m]
section = dict(fck=30.0, fyk=500.0, thickness=0.20, cover=0.04)

r04 = uls.eurocode2_shell_check(uls.ShellInput(**forces, **section))
r23 = uls2023.eurocode2_shell_check(uls2023.ShellInput(**forces, **section))

for name, r in (("2004", r04), ("2023", r23)):
    areas = [r.asx_bot, r.asy_bot, r.asx_top, r.asy_top]
    print(name, [f"{a * 1e4:.2f}" for a in areas], "cm²/m;",
          f"stirrups {r.asw_s * 1e4:.2f} cm²/m²;", "crushing:", r.crushing)

The four areas are the bars of the bottom and top faces in each direction; asw_s is the shear reinforcement. Faces without tension give zero: no minimum reinforcement is added.

# What each edition checked
r04.details["cracked"]          # LL (107): is the element cracked? (an uncracked one is not designed)
r04.details["shear"]["mode"]    # inner layer of Annex LL, with the chord force added to the outer layers
r23.details["method"]           # 'sandwich' (G.4(1)); 'optimum' (Tables G.2/G.3) when only moments act
r23.details["shear"]["tau_ed"], r23.details["shear"]["tau_rdc"]    # clause 8.2

Where the strut limits differ (ν, fcd) is where the editions part: try fck=60.0, or ask 2004 for the refined EN 1992-2 6.109 limit with strut_model="6.109". See Membranes, slabs and shells for the clauses.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The ec1 module provides tools for EN 1991 (Actions on Structures). It covers load type definitions, force representations, wind and snow sub-modules, and the full EN 1990 load combination engine.

docs.title: LoadType (enum)
docs.text:
Classifies an individual load for combination purposes.

Member Value Description PERMANENT 0 Self-weight, superimposed dead load LIVE 1 Imposed loads (occupancy) WIND 2 Wind action SNOW 3 Snow load EARTHQUAKE 4 Seismic action TEMPERATURE 5 Thermal action FIRE 6 Fire action ACCIDENTAL 7 Other accidental actions OTHER 8 —

docs.title: CombinationType (enum)
docs.text: Member Description ULS Ultimate Limit State (EN 1990 Eq. 6.10) ALS Accidental Limit State FLS Fatigue Limit State SLS_K SLS characteristic combination SLS_FR SLS frequent combination SLS_QP SLS quasi-permanent combination

docs.title: Load (dataclass)
docs.text:
Load(name, load_type, gamma_fav, gamma_unf, psi0, psi1, psi2, incombo=True)

A load carries its partial factors (favourable and unfavourable effect, EN 1990 Table A1.2) and its combination coefficients; it does not carry a value. incombo=False leaves it out of the combinations.

docs.title: Loads and the combinations
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec1 import Load, LoadType, Loads

loads = Loads()
#                  name  type                 γ fav  γ unf  ψ0   ψ1   ψ2
loads.add(Load("G", LoadType.PERMANENT, 1.0, 1.35, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
loads.add(Load("Q", LoadType.LIVE,      0.0, 1.50, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3))
loads.add(Load("W", LoadType.WIND,      0.0, 1.50, 0.6, 0.2, 0.0))

values = {"G": 20.0, "Q": 8.0, "W": 4.0}                 # characteristic values [kN/m²]

# ULS (EN 1990 Eq. 6.10): a dict {name: LoadCombination}; factors = {load name: (Load, factor)}
for name, combo in loads.get_ULS_combos().items():
    total = sum(factor * values[k] for k, (_, factor) in combo.factors.items())
    print(f"{name:34s} {total:7.2f}")

# SLS characteristic, frequent and quasi-permanent
for name, combo in loads.get_SLS_combos().items():
    print(name)

get_ULS_combos() and get_SLS_combos() return a dictionary {name: LoadCombination}. A LoadCombination has name, type (a CombinationType) and factors, a dictionary {load name: (Load, factor)}. LoadCombinations is a container of LoadCombination objects (add, remove, iteration).

docs.title: Force representations
docs.text:
Class Description BaseForce Abstract base class PlaneForce In-plane forces (Nx, Ny, Nxy) ShellForce Shell resultants (n_xx, n_yy, n_xy, m_xx, m_yy, m_xy, v_xz, v_yz) SlabForce Slab resultants (m_xx, m_yy, m_xy, v_xz, v_yz) FrameForce 1-D frame member forces (n_x, v_y, v_z, m_y, m_z, t_x) 
from eurocodepy.ec1 import ShellForce
f = ShellForce(n_xx=100.0, m_xx=20.0)     # kN, m by default: the unit system `u`
f.forces.shape, f.n_cases                 # (8, 1), 1

docs.title: ec1.wind
docs.text:
Functions of EN 1991-1-4 (4.2 to 4.5): v_b, c_r, c_o, s_coef, v_m, I_v, v_p, q_p. Heights and roughness lengths in m, velocities in m/s, pressures in N/m².

from eurocodepy.ec1 import wind

vb = wind.v_b(27.0)                                  # vb,0 = 27 m/s, cseason = cdir = 1
cr = wind.c_r(z=10, z_min=2, z_0=0.05, z_0II=0.05)   # terrain category II
co = wind.c_o(z=10)                                  # flat terrain
vm = wind.v_m(10, vb, cr, co)                        # mean wind velocity
qp = wind.q_p(10, vb, 2, 0.05, cr, co)               # peak velocity pressure [N/m²]

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The ec3 module provides tools for the design of steel structures according to EN 1993-1-1: material properties, standard rolled profiles, bolted and welded connections, section classification and the ULS section and member checks.

Profile properties are those of the catalogue: dimensions in cm, areas in cm², inertia in cm⁴. The checks take strengths in N/mm², forces in kN and moments in kNm, and read the geometry of a profile converting cm to mm.

docs.title: Steel
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec3 import Steel

steel = Steel('S355')
steel.fyk        # yield strength [MPa] (t ≤ 40 mm)
steel.fuk        # ultimate tensile strength [MPa]
steel.fyk40      # yield strength, 40 mm < t ≤ 80 mm
steel.Es         # elastic modulus [MPa]
steel.fyd        # design yield strength fyk/γM0
steel.gamma_M0, steel.gamma_M1, steel.gamma_M2

Grades (enum SteelEnum): S235, S275, S355, S450, and the others of the database.

docs.title: Bolts
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec3 import Bolt, BoltGrade

bolt = Bolt(20, '8.8')             # M20, grade 8.8
bolt.fub, bolt.fyb                 # ultimate and yield strength [MPa]
bolt.d, bolt.d0                    # nominal and hole diameter [mm]
bolt.A, bolt.Athread               # gross and tensile stress area As [cm²]

Grades: 4.6, 5.6, 6.6, 6.8, 8.8, 9.8, 10.9, 12.9 (BoltGrades, BoltsEnum). Bolt('M20', '8.8') reads the areas of the database; Bolt(20, '8.8') uses those of the standard size when it exists, 0,78·A otherwise, or the athread= you give.

docs.title: Weld
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec3 import Weld, WeldConnection, WeldTypeEnum

weld = Weld(a=5.0, length=200.0, steel_grade='S355')     # throat thickness a, length
group = WeldConnection()
group.add(weld)
group.total_length()
group.area, group.xg, group.yg                      # throat area and centroid [mm², mm]
group.inertia_xx, group.inertia_yy, group.inertia_xy  # about the centroid [mm⁴]
group.w_el_xx_sup, group.w_el_xx_inf                  # elastic moduli to the extreme welds [mm³]

WeldTypeEnum: SLIDE, SHEAR, NORMAL, SHEARNORMAL, SLIDENORMAL, SLIDESHEAR, SLINESHEARNORMAL.

docs.title: Steel profiles
docs.text:
ProfilesI, ProfilesCHS, ProfilesRHS and ProfilesSHS are dictionaries of the rolled profiles of the database, keyed by name; the profile classes hold the catalogue values.

from eurocodepy.ec3 import ProfilesI, ProfilesCHS, ProfilesRHS, ProfilesSHS

section = ProfilesI['IPE300']
section.h, section.b, section.tw, section.tf        # [cm]
section.A, section.Iy, section.Iz                   # [cm², cm⁴]
section.Wel_y, section.Wpl_y, section.Wel_z, section.Wpl_z    # [cm³]
section.IT, section.Iw, section.Av_z                # torsion, warping, shear area
section.Npl_Rd, section.Mpl_Rd_y, section.Vpl_Rd_z  # S235 resistances of the catalogue

list(ProfilesI)[:3]                                  # 'HEA100', 'HEA1000', 'HEA120'

I profiles: IPE, HEA, HEB, HEM; hollow sections: circular (CHS), rectangular (RHS) and square (SHS), with the enums ProfilesIEnum, ProfilesCHSEnum, ProfilesRHSEnum, ProfilesSHSEnum.

docs.title: SteelPlate
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec3 import SteelPlate

plate = SteelPlate(thickness=10.0, steel=steel, width=200.0)     # mm

docs.title: Bolted connections
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from eurocodepy.ec3 import BoltedConnection

conn = BoltedConnection(bolt, outer_plate=plate)
conn.Fv_Rd(), conn.Ft_Rd(), conn.Bp_Rd()           # shear, tension and punching resistance per bolt [kN]
r = conn.check(Fv_Ed=np.array([100.0]), Ft_Ed=np.array([0.0]))
r['ShearRatio'], r['BearingRatio'], r['TensileRatio'], r['PunchingRatio']

PinnedConnection and PinnedConnectionDouble add the bending of the pin (gap, M_Rd).

docs.title: Classification (EN 1993-1-1, 5.5)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec3 import classify_section

c = classify_section(section, fy=355.0, n_ed=0.0, m_ed=100.0)     # kN, kNm
c.section_class

docs.title: Section resistance (6.2)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec3 import section_check_profile, SectionForces

r = section_check_profile(section, 355.0, SectionForces(n_ed=0.0, my_ed=100.0, vz_ed=80.0))
r.utilization

eurocode3_section_check(SectionResistanceInput(...), SectionForces(...)) is the same check for a section described by its dimensions instead of a profile.

docs.title: Member buckling (6.3, Eqs. 6.61 and 6.62)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec3 import member_check_profile

r = member_check_profile(section, 355.0, n_ed=-200.0, my_ed=80.0,
                         lcr_y=4000.0, lcr_z=4000.0, l_lt=4000.0)      # buckling lengths [mm]
r.utilization

eurocode3_member_check(MemberInput(...)) takes the section properties directly. All the checks accept trace= (a CalcReport) to record the steps.

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text: Calculations follow EN 1993-1-1:2005 and EN 1993-1-8 (connections).

docs.title: Further reading
docs.text: • EN 1993-1-1 — Design of steel structures

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The ec5 module provides tools for the design of timber structures according to EN 1995-1-1: material classes, modification factors, ULS checks and floor vibration. The ULS checks exist for the 2004 edition (ec5.uls) and for the second generation (ec5.uls2025, EN 1995-1-1:2025, clause 8); both have the same functions and can be swapped.

Units: forces in kN, moments in kNm, section dimensions in m, effective lengths in mm, strengths in MPa.

docs.title: Timber and its products
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec5.materials import SolidTimber, Glulam

t = SolidTimber("C24")
t.fmk      # characteristic bending strength [MPa]
t.ft0k     # tension parallel to grain
t.fc0k     # compression parallel to grain
t.fvk      # shear
t.E0mean   # mean modulus parallel to grain [MPa]
t.E0k      # 5th percentile modulus [MPa]
t.Gmean    # mean shear modulus [MPa]
t.rhok     # characteristic density [kg/m³]
t.rhom     # mean density [kg/m³]
t.safety   # γM (Table 2.3)

g = Glulam("GL28h")        # GL20h … GL32h (homogeneous) and GL20c … GL32c (combined)
Class Product SolidTimber (alias ST, Softwood, Hardwood) sawn timber, strength classes C and D Glulam (alias GL) glued laminated timber CLT, LVL not implemented (the grade tables are missing)

docs.title: ServiceClass and LoadDuration
docs.text: ServiceClass: SC1, SC2, SC3, SC4. LoadDuration: Permanent, LongDuration, MediumDuration, ShortDuration, Instantaneous.

docs.title: k_mod and design values
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec5.materials import ServiceClass, LoadDuration

kmod = t.k_mod(ServiceClass.SC1, LoadDuration.MediumDuration)       # 0.8 (Table 3.1)
d = t.design_values(ServiceClass.SC1, LoadDuration.MediumDuration)   # fmd, ft0d, fc0d, fvd, fc90d, ft90d, kmod, safety
d["fmd"]                                                            # kmod·fmk/γM [MPa]

GetTimberDesignValues(timber, combos, service_class=ServiceClass.SC1) returns the design values of each combination of a Loads: kmod is that of the shortest action in the combination (EN 1995-1-1, 3.1.3(2)), attributes["loadduration"] of a LoadCombination overrides it, and serviceability combinations give {"design": False}.

from eurocodepy.ec1 import Load, LoadType, Loads
from eurocodepy.ec5.materials import GetTimberDesignValues

loads = Loads()
loads.add(Load("G", LoadType.PERMANENT, 1.0, 1.35, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
loads.add(Load("W", LoadType.WIND, 0.0, 1.5, 0.6, 0.2, 0.0))
values = GetTimberDesignValues(t, loads.get_ULS_combos().values(), ServiceClass.SC2)
{name: v["kmod"] for name, v in values.items()}          # short-term kmod in the combinations with wind

docs.title: Section check (N, My, Mz, Vy, Vz, T)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec5.materials import SolidTimber, ServiceClass, LoadDuration
from eurocodepy.ec5.uls import TimberSectionInput, TimberForces, eurocode5_section_check
from eurocodepy.utils import RectangularCrossSection

section = RectangularCrossSection(0.10, 0.20)                       # b, h [m]
inp = TimberSectionInput(section, SolidTimber("C24"), ServiceClass.SC1, LoadDuration.MediumDuration,
                         l_0y=3000.0, l_0z=3000.0, l_0m=3000.0)     # effective lengths [mm]
r = eurocode5_section_check(inp, TimberForces(n_ed=-20.0, my_ed=5.0, vz_ed=8.0))   # n_ed < 0: compression
r.utilization, r.passed
r.util_bending_axial, r.util_shear, r.util_torsion
r.k_c, r.k_m

docs.title: Single checks
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec5.uls import calc_k_c, calc_k_m, calc_k_red, calc_mcr

kc_y, kc_z = calc_k_c(3000.0, 3000.0, section, SolidTimber("C24"))   # column instability, §6.3.2
km = calc_k_m(3000.0, section, SolidTimber("C24"))                    # lateral-torsional buckling, §6.3.3

check_bending_with_normal (bending with axial force, §6.2.3 and §6.2.4) and check_shear_with_torsion (§6.1.7) are the two parts of the section check and return a dictionary. get_safety_factor("timber") gives γM for a product (timber, glulam, lvl, clt, …).

docs.title: Tapered and curved beams
docs.text:
check_tapered_edge(m_ed, b, h, alpha, tension_on_cut_edge, timber) (§6.4.2) and check_apex_zone(ApexInput(...), timber) (§6.4.3) with the factors calc_k_l, calc_k_p, calc_k_r, calc_k_vol, calc_k_m_alpha.

from eurocodepy.ec5.materials import Glulam
from eurocodepy.ec5.uls import check_tapered_edge

r = check_tapered_edge(10.0, 0.10, 0.30, 0.10, True, Glulam("GL28h"))   # m_ed, b, h, α [rad]
r.util

docs.title: Vibration — ec5.sls.vibration
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec5.sls.vibration import floor_freq, vel, vlim, a_from_b, b_from_a

f1 = floor_freq(l=5.0, EI=1.2e5, m=50.0)                          # fundamental frequency [Hz]
v = vel(f1, b=3.0, l=5.0, m=50.0, EIl=1.2e5, EIt=1.0e3)          # unit impulse velocity response [m/(N·s)]
a_from_b(100.0), b_from_a(1.0)                                    # Figure 7.2 coefficients a and b

vlim(f1, b, damp) is the limit of the velocity response. ec5.sls.deformation is a placeholder.

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text: Calculations follow EN 1995-1-1:2004+A2:2014 and, in uls2025, EN 1995-1-1:2025.

docs.title: Further reading
docs.text: • EN 1995-1-1 — Design of timber structures

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The ec7 module provides tools for geotechnical design according to EN 1997-1: soil definitions, partial factors of the design approaches, bearing resistance of shallow foundations (static and seismic, EN 1998-5) and earth pressure coefficients.

Angles are in radians in the calculation functions (bearing_resistance, seismic_bearing_resistance, pressure_coefficients). Soil(friction_angle=30.0) takes degrees and stores radians.

docs.title: Soil and SoilEnum
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec7 import Soil, SoilEnum

soil = Soil("Dense sand", unit_weight=19.0, friction_angle=34.0, cohesion=0.0)   # degrees, kN/m³, kPa
soil.unit_weight, soil.friction_angle, soil.cohesion          # friction_angle in radians
soil.is_drained, soil.is_coherent, soil.young, soil.poiss, soil.ks, soil.sig_adm

SoilEnum.Sand, SoilEnum.Clay, SoilEnum.Gravel, SoilEnum.Rock   # typical soils

docs.title: SoilSafetyFactors and SoilSafetyFactorsEnum
docs.text:
Partial factors of the geotechnical design approaches (EN 1997-1).

from eurocodepy.ec7 import SoilSafetyFactorsEnum

sf = SoilSafetyFactorsEnum.STRGEO_A2
sf.phi, sf.c, sf.cu, sf.gamma                  # on tan φ', c', cu and γ
sf.perm_unfav, sf.var_unfav                    # on actions
sf.bearing, sf.slide                           # on resistances

Members (each is a SoilSafetyFactors): EQU, EQU_ACC, STRGEO_A1, STRGEO_A2, STRGEO_B, STRGEO_C, STRGEO_ACC, STRGEO_SLS.

docs.title: Seismic parameters
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec7 import get_soil_seismic_parameters, soil_gamma_rd

params = get_soil_seismic_parameters("S1", "PT", "C", "ii", "PT1", "1_2")   # name, code, soil, class, spectrum, zone
params.alpha, params.smax, params.avg_ahg, params.r
params.kh, params.kv                             # horizontal and vertical seismic coefficients

soil_gamma_rd["compact sand"]                    # γRd by soil type: 1.0, 1.15, 1.5 …

docs.title: SoilSurcharge
docs.text: SoilSurcharge(q=10.0, psi0=0.6, psi1=0.4, psi2=0.2): a surcharge on the soil surface with its combination coefficients.

docs.title: Bearing resistance — ec7.bearing_capacity
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from eurocodepy.ec7 import bearing_resistance, seismic_bearing_resistance

phi = np.radians(30.0)

# EN 1997-1: effective width Bx, length By, horizontal loads Hx, Hy and vertical load N
# [m, kN], effective friction angle, unit weight [kN/m³], surcharge beside the footing q [kPa], cohesion c
q = 0.8 * 18.0
r = bearing_resistance(Bx=1.5, By=2.0, Hx=20.0, Hy=0.0, N=200.0, phi=phi, gamma=18.0, q=q, c=0.0)

# EN 1998-5: True where the verification is satisfied (two vertical directions)
ok = seismic_bearing_resistance(ag=0.2, avg_ahg=0.5, S=1.4, B=1.5, H=20.0, N=200.0, M=10.0,
                                phi=phi, gamma_s=18.0)            # cu=..., soil_type="coherent" for clays

bearing_resistance also takes arrays (one value per combination).

docs.title: Earth pressures — ec7.earth_pressures
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from eurocodepy.ec7 import pressure_coefficients, EarthPressureModels

phi, delta = np.radians(30.0), np.radians(15.0)      # soil and wall friction angles
theta, beta = 0.0, 0.0                                # backfill slope and wall inclination
Ka, Kp, Kaq, Kpq, dkas1, dkps1, dkas2, dkps2 = pressure_coefficients(
    phi, delta, theta, beta, method=EarthPressureModels.COULOMB)

Methods (EarthPressureModels): RANKINE, COULOMB, EC7 (the default) and INREST. Kaq and Kpq are the coefficients at rest; dkas* and dkps* the seismic increments of EN 1998-5 when seismic= (a SoilSeismicParameters) is given.

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text: Calculations follow EN 1997-1:2004. Seismic bearing resistance follows EN 1998-5.

docs.title: Further reading
docs.text: • EN 1997-1 — Geotechnical design

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The ec8 module provides tools for seismic design according to EN 1998-1. It generates elastic and design response spectra, retrieves national annex parameters for both the standard Eurocode and the Portuguese National Annex, and exports spectra to CSV.

docs.title: Response spectra — ec8.spectrum
docs.text: Accelerations are in m/s² (a_g, and the ordinates of the spectra); periods in s.

docs.title: get_spec_params
docs.text:
Returns the spectrum parameters (S, a_g, T_B, T_C, T_D) for a locale, code, importance class, soil type and seismic zone. a_g = a_gR·γI; S is interpolated between S_max and S_min with a_g.

from eurocodepy.ec8 import get_spec_params

s_val, a_g, t_b, t_c, t_d = get_spec_params(
    locale="PT",        # "EU" (CEN) or "PT" (Portuguese National Annex)
    code="PT1",         # see the table below
    class_imp="II",     # importance class: I, II, III, IV
    soil="C",           # soil type: A, B, C, D, E
    zone="1_2",         # seismic zone (code-dependent)
)

docs.title: Available codes
docs.text: locale code Description EU CEN_1 Standard Eurocode type 1 spectrum EU CEN_2 Standard Eurocode type 2 spectrum PT PT1 Portuguese NA — type 1 (continental Portugal) PT PT2 Portuguese NA — type 2 PT PTA Portuguese NA — Azores

docs.title: Seismic zones
docs.text:
• PT1: 1_1, 1_2, 1_3, 1_4, 1_5, 1_6
  • PT2 / PTA: 2_1, 2_2, 2_3, 2_4, 2_5
  • CEN_1 / CEN_2: .1g, .2g, … .9g, 1_0g (the reference acceleration as a fraction of g)

docs.title: get_spectrum_ec8
docs.text:
Builds the horizontal design spectrum as a pandas.DataFrame with columns period and value.

from eurocodepy.ec8 import get_spectrum_ec8

spec = get_spectrum_ec8(
    locale="PT",
    code="PT1",
    imp_class="II",
    soil="C",
    zone="1_2",
    behaviour=3.0,   # behaviour factor q
)
spec.columns.tolist()       # ['period', 'value']
spec["value"].max()         # largest design ordinate [m/s²]

docs.title: get_spectrum_user and get_elastic_spectrum_user
docs.text:
Spectra from arbitrary parameters, without a National Annex entry.

from eurocodepy.ec8 import get_spectrum_user, get_elastic_spectrum_user

# a_g [m/s²], S, q, T_B, T_C, T_D
design = get_spectrum_user(a_g=2.0, s_val=1.15, q=4.0, t_b=0.1, t_c=0.6, t_d=2.0)
elastic = get_elastic_spectrum_user(a_g=2.0, s_val=1.15, t_b=0.1, t_c=0.6, t_d=2.0, damping=5.0)

docs.title: calc_spectrum, calc_elastic_spectrum, damping_correction
docs.text:
Ordinates of one period, from already-extracted parameters (EN 1998-1, Eqs. 3.2 to 3.5 and 3.13 to 3.16).

from eurocodepy.ec8 import calc_spectrum, calc_elastic_spectrum, damping_correction

sd = calc_spectrum(0.3, a_g=2.0, s_val=1.15, q=3.0, t_b=0.1, t_c=0.6, t_d=2.0)   # design
se = calc_elastic_spectrum(0.3, 2.0, 1.15, 0.1, 0.6, 2.0)                       # elastic, 5 % damping
eta = damping_correction(5.0)                                                    # 1.0

get_spectrum_parameters(code, coef_imp, soil, zone) is the same lookup as get_spec_params with the tables inside the function (codes CEN-1, CEN-2, PT-1, PT-2, PT-A, hyphenated); prefer get_spec_params.

docs.title: draw_spectrum_ec8
docs.text:
Plots the spectrum with matplotlib.

from eurocodepy.ec8 import draw_spectrum_ec8

draw_spectrum_ec8(spec, show=False, save=True, filename="spectrum.png")

docs.title: write_spectrum_ec8
docs.text:
Exports the spectrum to a text file (two columns, period and value).

from eurocodepy.ec8 import write_spectrum_ec8

write_spectrum_ec8(spec, filename="spectrum_PT1_II_C_1_2.csv", separator=",")

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text: Calculations follow EN 1998-1:2004 and the Portuguese National Annex (NP EN 1998-1).

docs.title: Further reading
docs.text: • EN 1998-1 — Design for earthquake resistance

docs.title: Editions and National Annexes
docs.text: EurocodePy keeps the values of a Eurocode edition and of each National Annex as data, not as code. Functions that depend on the edition take edition= and those that depend on Nationally Determined Parameters (NDPs) take annex= as well.

docs.title: Editions
docs.text:
eurocodes.json holds the recommended values of the 2004 edition (the default, edition=None) and, under Editions, the changes of other editions:

"Editions": {"ec2": {"2023": {
    "overrides": {"Concrete.Grade": {}, "Concrete.Parameters": {}},   // dot-paths replacing 2004 data
    "partial_factors": {},         // sibling sections: Tables 4.1 to 4.3
    "punch_params": {}, "shear_interface": {}, "detailing": {}, "creep_shrinkage": {}
}}}

from eurocodepy import dbase, ec2

dbase.get_edition_data("ec2", "2023")                          # {"Concrete": {"Grade", "Parameters"}, ...}
dbase.get_edition_params("ec2", "partial_factors", "2023")     # a sibling section
ec2.get_concrete("C30/37", edition="2023", situation="accidental")

get_concrete accepts a grade name, a ConcreteClass or a Concrete; a Concrete of another edition is refused rather than silently converted. The 2023 edition has the grades of Table 5.1 (C12/15 to C100/115); 2004 has C12/15 to C90/105.

docs.title: National Annexes
docs.text:
An annex is a patch with the same shape as an Editions entry, kept in its own file (data/national_annexes/<COUNTRY>.json) and deep-merged over the recommended values. PT is built in; the package only ships values it can source and never invents an annex.

What the Portuguese annex contains

PT.json has the loads (wind, seismic and live-load data of Portugal) and, so far, no patch of EN 1992-1-1:2023: annex="PT" in Concrete, material_partial_factors, detailing, … returns the values recommended by the Eurocode, the same as annex=None. The NDPs of the Portuguese annex for the 2023 edition still have to be added (see register_annex to do it yourself) and must be checked against the published annex before design use.

Function Purpose available_annexes() codes of the loaded annexes get_annex(code) the annex's data register_annex(source, replace=False) add an annex (file path or dict) and return its code unregister_annex(code) remove it 
import eurocodepy as ec

ec.register_annex({
    "country": "XX",
    "editions": {"ec2": {"2023": {"partial_factors": {"materials": {"persistent": {"gamma_c": 1.4}}}}}},
    "loads": {"wind": {}, "seismic": {}, "live": {}},   # optional: next to the "EU" data
})
ec.ec2.Concrete("C30/37", edition="2023", annex="XX").gamma_c   # 1.4
ec.ec2.Concrete("C30/37", edition="2023").gamma_c               # 1.5, annex=None: the Eurocode
ec.unregister_annex("XX")

An unknown code raises ValueError listing the available ones. The loads of an annex are merged into db["Loads"], so wind_get_params, seismic_get_params and the EC1/EC7/EC8 functions find the country.

docs.title: dbobj is deprecated
docs.text:
eurocodepy.dbobj was a snapshot of db with attribute access, built at import, so it did not follow annexes registered later. It is now built only when asked for, with a DeprecationWarning, and will be removed in 2028. Use dictionary access on db, or the edition-aware functions:

Before Now dbobj.Materials.Concrete.Grade db["Materials"]["Concrete"]["Grade"] dbobj.Loads.Wind... db["Loads"]["Wind"][...] the 2023 tables, by hand dbase.get_edition_data("ec2", "2023", annex=...) a section of an edition dbase.get_edition_params("ec2", "detailing", "2023", annex=...)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The utils module provides cross-cutting helper functions for geometric, mechanical, and mathematical operations commonly needed in structural calculations. It is used internally throughout EurocodePy and is also part of the public API.

docs.title: Cross sections — utils.crosssection
docs.text:
RectangularCrossSection(width, height) and CircularCrossSection(diameter) give the geometric properties of a section (lengths in the unit of the arguments).

from eurocodepy.utils import RectangularCrossSection, CircularCrossSection

r = RectangularCrossSection(0.30, 0.60)       # m
r.area, r.inertia_y, r.inertia_z               # A, Iy, Iz
r.bend_mod_y, r.bend_mod_z                     # Wy, Wz
r.radius_y, r.radius_z                         # radii of gyration
r.torsional_inertia, r.torsion_modulus, r.polar_inertia
r.shape                                        # CrossSectionShape member

CircularCrossSection(0.40).area

These objects are what the EC5 checks (ec5.uls) take as section.

docs.title: Reinforced and prestressed sections — utils.section_properties
docs.text:
calc_section_rectangular and calc_section_T return the uncracked and the cracked properties (area, centroid, inertia, section moduli, neutral axis) of a section with passive and prestressed reinforcement, with the steel homogenised by alpha_Es and alpha_Ep. The arguments are consistent units (here m, m², kNm and kN). calc_section_T_uncrack and calc_section_T_crack give each of them separately.

import numpy as np
from eurocodepy.utils import calc_section_rectangular

arr = lambda *v: np.array(v)
uncracked, cracked = calc_section_rectangular(
    h=0.50, b=0.30,
    A_s=arr(8.0e-4), A_sc=arr(0.0), A_p=arr(0.0),      # tension, compression, prestressing steel
    ds=arr(0.46), dsc=arr(0.04), dp=arr(0.50),        # their distances to the top fibre
    alpha_Es=15.0, alpha_Ep=15.0,
    M=arr(150.0), P=arr(0.001),
)
uncracked["Area"], uncracked["Inertia"]
cracked["NeutralAxis"], cracked["Inertia"], cracked["zGs"], cracked["zGi"]

docs.title: Stress calculations — utils.stress
docs.text:
The six components of the stress tensor are sigxx, sigyy, sigzz, sigxy, sigyz, sigzx.

from eurocodepy.utils import stress

# Principal stresses (ascending) and the normalised principal directions (columns)
values, vectors = stress.principals(10.0, 5.0, 0.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0)

# Principal vectors scaled by the principal stresses
stress.principal_vectors(10.0, 5.0, 0.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0)

# Invariants: I1, J2, J3, mean stress, equivalent (von Mises) stress, Lode r, z, θ, cos 3θ, triaxiality
i1, j2, j3, mean, eqv, lode_r, lode_z, lode_theta, cos3t, triax = stress.invariants(
    10.0, 5.0, 0.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0)

FailureCriteria is an enum of the criteria available (VON_MISES, MOHR_COULOMB, RANKINE, CONCRETE, …).

docs.title: Usage in other modules
docs.text:
The utils module is re-exported at the top level of eurocodepy:

import eurocodepy as ec

ec.crosssection          # the module utils.crosssection
ec.section_properties    # the module utils.section_properties
ec.stress                # the module utils.stress

docs.title: Further reading
docs.text: • eurocodepy Documentation

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The ec2 module provides tools for the design of reinforced and prestressed concrete structures according to EN 1992-1-1 and, for slabs and shells, EN 1992-2 Annex LL. It supports the 2004 edition and the 2023 edition (second generation) where functions have been updated; see Editions and National Annexes.

Page Content this page conventions, materials, helper functions, limitations EN 1992-1-1:2004 beam bending and shear, anchorage, punching, SLS crack, creep, shrinkage, fire EN 1992-1-1:2023 shear (8.2), torsion (8.3), detailing (12), creep and shrinkage (Annex B) Membranes, slabs and shells Annex G (2023), EN 1992-1-1 Annex F and EN 1992-2 6.109 and Annex LL (2004), sandwich model, out-of-plane shear Clause map every function of uls2023 by clause and equation (generated from the docstrings)

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Functions written for the second-generation code (uls2023, time_dependent2023, and the shell, slab and membrane checks) use kN, m and MPa unless the docstring says otherwise. The older 2004 functions were written one by one and mix units; the table below is what each family expects.

Family Lengths Areas Forces / moments Stresses uls2023, uls.shell_check, uls.slab_check, uls.membrane_check m m² (per m: m²/m) kN, kN/m, kNm, kNm/m MPa uls.beam (calc_mrd, calc_asl) m cm² kN·m MPa uls.shear (calc_vrd, calc_vrdc, calc_asws) m m² per m kN MPa uls.shell (calc_reinf_plane, calc_reinf_shell) m forces, see the docstring kN/m — uls.punch mm — kN, kNm MPa uls.anchorage mm mm² N MPa sls.crack m (bar diameter too) m² kNm MPa; crack_opening returns mm time_dependent2023, sls.creep, sls.shrinkage hn in mm — — MPa; ages in days

Signs. Tension and sagging bending are positive in the code of 2023 (Annex G): the bottom layer of uls2023 is in tension for positive m. EN 1992-2 Annex LL and uls.shell.calc_reinf_shell take positive m as tension on the top face. uls.shell_check hides this by returning asx_bot, asy_bot, asx_top, asy_top for the physical faces. Axial force is positive in tension, except in sls.crack.crack_opening (compression positive, see its docstring).

docs.title: Concrete
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2 import Concrete

c = Concrete('C30/37')
c.fck      # characteristic compressive strength [MPa]
c.fcd      # design compressive strength (fck / γc)
c.fctm     # mean tensile strength
c.Ecm      # secant modulus of elasticity [MPa]

Available grades: 2004, C12/15 to C90/105; 2023 (Table 5.1), C12/15 to C100/115.

docs.title: EN 1992-1-1:2023
docs.text:
c = Concrete('C30/37', edition='2023')                  # k_tc = 1.0 (late loading)
c = Concrete('C50/60', edition='2023', loading='other') # k_tc = 0.85
c.eta_cc, c.k_tc, c.fcd   # fcd = eta_cc * k_tc * fck / gamma_c  (Eq. 5.3)
Concrete('C30/37', edition='2023', situation='accidental').gamma_c   # 1.15 (Table 4.3)
Concrete('C30/37', edition='2023', k_cip=1.1)           # cast in the ground (4.3.3(4))

from eurocodepy.ec2 import material_partial_factors, prestress_partial_factors
material_partial_factors('2023', 'fatigue')   # gamma_s, gamma_c, gamma_ce, gamma_v
prestress_partial_factors('2023')             # Tables 4.1 and 4.2

loading='late' is t_ref ≤ 28 d (CN/CR) or 56 d (CS) with the design loading not expected for 3 months after casting; 'other' is every other case, including fck(t). Reinforcement and Prestress take edition and situation as well. The edition=None default is 2004.

The check inputs (PunchInput, ShearInput, SlabInput, MembraneInput, ShearTorsionInput) take the partial factors of a design situation with from_partial_factors:

from eurocodepy.ec2.uls.punch_check import PunchInput
inp = PunchInput.from_partial_factors("2023", "accidental", d=0.25, bx=0.4, by=0.4, fck=30, fyk=500)
inp.gamma_v, inp.gamma_c, inp.gamma_s, inp.edition   # 1.15, 1.15, 1.0, '2023'

Convenience instances are pre-created: C20_25, C25_30, C30_37, …, C90_105.

docs.title: Reinforcement
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2 import Reinforcement

r = Reinforcement('B500B')
r.fyk     # characteristic yield strength [MPa]
r.fyd     # design yield strength (fyk / γs)
r.Es      # elastic modulus [MPa]

Available grades: B400A/B/C, B500A/B/C, B600A/B/C, B700A/B/C, A400NR, A500NR, A400NRSD, A500NRSD, A500EL.

docs.title: Prestress
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2 import Prestress
p = Prestress('Y1860S7 12.5')   # class and nominal diameter
p.fpk     # characteristic tensile strength [MPa]
p.fp0_1k  # 0.1% proof strength [MPa]

docs.title: Helper functions
docs.text:
# Partial safety factors
from eurocodepy.ec2 import GammaC, GammaS, GammaCT, GammaP   # 1.5, 1.15, 1.5, 1.15 (floats)

# Time-dependent concrete strength factor
from eurocodepy.ec2 import beta_cc
s = beta_cc(t=28, s=0.25)   # βcc(t) of Eq. 3.2: 1.0 at 28 days, s = 0.25 for class N cement

# Creep and shrinkage (EN 1992-1-1:2004, Annex B)
from eurocodepy.ec2 import calc_creep_coef, calc_shrink_strain

# Creep and shrinkage (EN 1992-1-1:2023, Annex B): same model as ec2.time_dependent2023, validated
from eurocodepy.ec2 import creep_coef, shrink_strain

docs.title: Not implemented
docs.text:
• EN 1992-1-1:2023: uls2023.column is the 2004 column code with the 2023 fcd; SLS crack width (sls.crack) and anchorage and lap lengths (uls.anchorage) are still 2004.
  • EN 1992-2 Annex LL: the general eccentric case of (108) (zn ≠ zt) and the eccentric reinforcement of (115)c.
  • EN 1992-1-1:2004 slabs: the chord force of the shear truss is not added to the Wood-Armer bars (the sandwich model adds it).
  • Minimum reinforcement is never added to membrane, slab and shell designs unless min_reinf asks for it (default "demand": a face with no tension gets zero).

docs.title: Bending — ec2.uls.beam
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2 import Concrete, Reinforcement
from eurocodepy.ec2.uls.beam import calc_mrd, calc_asl, get_bend_params

c, s = Concrete("C30/37"), Reinforcement("B500B")
b, d = 0.30, 0.46                                  # m

# Design bending resistance of a rectangular section: As in cm²
mrd, eps_s, x = calc_mrd(b, d, 8.04, c.fcd, s.fyd)     # kNm, steel strain [‰], x/d
# Required tensile reinforcement for MEd = 150 kNm
asl, eps_s, x = calc_asl(b, d, 150.0, c.fcd, s.fyd)      # cm², steel strain [‰], x/d
# Stress-block parameters of a concrete class
get_bend_params("C30/37")

docs.title: Anchorage and lap lengths — ec2.uls.anchorage
docs.text:
Ribbed bars, EN 1992-1-1:2004 §8.4 and §8.7. Units: mm, mm², MPa (the units of the bond clauses themselves).

from eurocodepy.ec2.uls import (
    bond_conditions_beam, beam_cover_distance,
    design_anchorage_length, lap_length,
)

bond = bond_conditions_beam(h=500, face="top")            # "poor" (h > 250 mm)
cd = beam_cover_distance(width=300, cover=38, n_bars=4, phi=16)   # Fig. 8.3

a = design_anchorage_length(phi=16, fck=30, fyk=500, cd=cd,
                            good_bond=(bond == "good"))
a["fbd"], a["lb_rqd"], a["lbd"]          # bond stress, basic and design length
l = lap_length(phi=16, fck=30, fyk=500, cd=cd, rho1=50)
l["alpha6"], l["l0"]                     # lap length of Eq. 8.10
  • bond_strength — f_bd = 2.25·η1·η2·f_ctd (§8.4.2; f_ctd capped at C60/75).
  • basic_anchorage_length — l_b,rqd = (φ/4)·σ_sd/f_bd (Eq. 8.3).
  • anchorage_coefficients — α1 … α5 of Table 8.2 (shape, cover, confinement, welded bars, transverse pressure; α2·α3·α5 ≥ 0.7).
  • design_anchorage_length — l_bd = α1·α2·α3·α4·α5·l_b,rqd ≥ l_b,min (Eq. 8.4, 8.6, 8.7); σ_sd defaults to f_yd (the safe choice for a curtailed bar).
  • lap_length — l_0 = α1·α2·α3·α5·α6·l_b,rqd ≥ l_0,min (Eq. 8.10, 8.11), α6 = √(ρ1/25) between 1 and 1.5 (Table 8.3).

Every function accepts trace= (a CalcReport) to record the steps.

docs.title: EN 1992-1-1:2023
docs.text: Second-generation Eurocode 2. Materials, partial factors and get_concrete(edition="2023") are on the main page; membranes, slabs and shells (Annex G) are in Membranes, slabs and shells. Units: kN, m, MPa.

docs.title: Shear, EN 1992-1-1:2023 (Clause 8.2)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2 import uls2023

inp = uls2023.ShearInput(b=0.3, d=0.5, fck=30, fyk=500, as_long=0.0015)   # m, MPa, m²
r = uls2023.eurocode2_shear_check(inp, v_ed=150.0)                          # kN
r.mode, r.asw_s, r.cot, r.vrd_c, r.vrd_max   # 'stirrups', Asw/s [m²/m], cot θ, ...

uls2023.shear.calc_taurdc(rho_l=0.01, fck=30, d=0.5, fyd=434.8)   # τRd,c, Eq. (8.27)
uls2023.shear.calc_tau_rdi(30, 1.5, 20, "rough", sigma_n=1.0)     # interface, Eq. (8.76)

The check follows 8.2.1: τEd ≤ τRdc,min (verification omitted), τEd ≤ τRd,c (no calculated reinforcement), otherwise the compression field with ν = 0,5 and the flattest strut that does not crush (cot θ ≤ cot θmin). ShearInput takes gamma_v (Table 4.3), n_ed/m_ed (shear span and axial force, 8.2.2(3)-(4)) and asw_min_s, the minimum Asw/s (default ρw,min of Eq. 12.4; 0.0 omits it). The formulae for the other parts of 8.2 (planar members, strain-based ν, chord forces, web-flange shear, interfaces) are in uls2023.shear.

docs.title: Torsion and shear + torsion, EN 1992-1-1:2023 (Clause 8.3)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2 import uls2023

t = uls2023.calc_torsion(30.0, 0.3, 0.5, 30.0, 1.5, 500.0, 1.15, 2.0, cover=0.05)
t["Asw_tor_s"], t["Asl_tor"], t["TRd_max"]      # Eqs. (8.82), (8.83), (8.84)

inp = uls2023.ShearTorsionInput(b=0.3, h=0.5, cover=0.05, fck=30, fyk=500, as_long=0.0015)
r = uls2023.eurocode2_shear_torsion_check(inp, v_ed=150.0, t_ed=30.0)
r.asw_total_s, r.asl_tor_total, r.interaction   # interaction: Eq. (8.86)

cot θ is shared by shear and torsion; 1/2,5 ≤ cot θ ≤ 2,5 (Eq. 8.85). ν of Eq. (8.84) comes from Annex G: 0,60 at cot θ = 1, otherwise Eq. (G.9) with ε1 = max(G.10, G.11) and the steel strain fyd/Es (0,38 at cot θ = 2, 0,29 at cot θ = 2,5); nu= overrides it. For a squat section (bmax/bmin < 1,5) the cover is reduced to 0,07·bmin (8.3.4(5)).

docs.title: Creep, shrinkage and relaxation, EN 1992-1-1:2023 (Annex B)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2 import time_dependent2023 as td

fcm = 38.0                                                      # C30/37, fcm,28
td.creep_coefficient(18250 + 28, 28, fcm, rh=50, hn=200, cls="CN")   # φ(50 y, 28 d) ≈ 2,46
td.shrinkage_total(18251, 1, fcm, rh=50, hn=200, cls="CN")           # εcs after 50 years of drying
td.fcm_t(7, fcm, 30.0, "CN"); td.ecm_t(7, 33000.0, 30.0, "CN")       # strength and stiffness at 7 days
td.creep_coefficient_50y(28, "CN", 50, 200, 30.0)                    # Table 5.2, any fck by (35/fck)^A
td.relaxation_loss(18250, 1000.0, td.relaxation_rho1000(0.7, "wire"))  # Eq. (B.43), MPa

Ages in days, hn = 2Ac/u in mm, RH in %. cls is the strength development class CS, CN or CR (Table B.1). ec2.sls.creep.creep_coef and ec2.sls.shrinkage.shrink_strain are this model (same results, arrays accepted).

docs.title: Detailing, EN 1992-1-1:2023 (Clause 12)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2.uls2023 import detailing as dt

dt.calc_asw_min_s(f_ck=30, f_yk=500, b_w=0.3, ductility="B")   # Eq. (12.4), m²/m
dt.beam_max_spacings(d=0.5)                                  # Table 12.1: s_l_max, s_bu_max, s_tr_max
dt.column_min_longitudinal(n_ed=2000, f_yd=434.8, a_c=0.09)   # Table 12.3, m²
dt.wall_min_vertical(a_c=0.2, f_ctm=2.9, f_yk=500)            # Table 12.4, m²
dt.calc_vrd_int(a_s_int=1e-3, f_yd=434.8, ductility="B")      # Eq. (12.10), kN

The tables of Clause 12 are NDPs; the functions return the values of the Eurocode.

docs.title: Membranes, slabs and shells
docs.text: Units: kN, m, MPa. See the conventions for signs.

docs.title: EN 1992-1-1:2023, Annex G
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2 import uls2023
from eurocodepy.ec2.uls2023 import annex_g as g

g.membrane_optimum(5.0, 3.0, 2.0)          # Table G.1: cot θ*, ftdx*, ftdy*, σcd*
r = uls2023.eurocode2_membrane_check(
    uls2023.MembraneInput(n_xx=100, n_yy=50, n_xy=20, fck=30, fyk=500, thickness=0.2))
r.asx, r.asy, r.crushing                    # σcd ≤ ν·fcd (ν = 0,4, or nu_mode="strain")

s = uls2023.slab_design.eurocode2_slab_check(uls2023.slab_design.SlabInput(
    m_x=50, m_y=30, m_xy=10, fck=30, fyk=500, thickness=0.2,
    cover_bot_x=0.03, cover_bot_y=0.04, cover_top_x=0.03, cover_top_y=0.04))
s.asx_bot, s.details["m_rdx"]               # Tables G.2/G.3 optimum capacities

Tension and sagging moments are positive. slab_design takes the design moments of the element (it is not a drop-in for uls.slab_check, which takes Wood-Armer moments). SlabInput.method is "auto" (default): Tables G.2/G.3 where |mxy| < 0,07·d²·fcd and nEd = 0, the sandwich model (G.4(1)) otherwise — two layers t = 2·c apart by z = h − t, each designed as a membrane, σcd ≤ ν·fcd checked per layer (details["crushing"]); "optimum" and "sandwich" force one of them. In-plane forces go in n_x, n_y, n_xy.

docs.title: EN 1992-1-1:2004 and EN 1992-2 (Annex F, 6.109, Annex LL)
Slabs and membranes
docs.text:
uls.slab_check takes Wood-Armer moments (SlabInput.min_reinf="demand" by default: a face with no tension gets zero reinforcement). strip_reinforcement is the underlying strip design. The 2004 code does not limit mxy; the Wood-Armer tables of EN 1992-1-1:2023 (G.4(5)) are valid for |mxy| ≤ 0,07·d²·fcd.

uls.eurocode2_membrane_check limits the concrete strut with MembraneInput.strut_model:

from eurocodepy.ec2.uls import shell

sx, sy, txy, fck, fcd, cot = -10.0, -5.0, 2.0, 30.0, 20.0, 2.0      # MPa
shell.strut_limit("annex_f", sx, sy, txy, fck, fcd, cot)     # F.1(3)-(4): σ ≤ fcd, or ν·fcd, ν = 0,6(1 − fck/250)
shell.strut_limit("6.109", sx, sy, txy, fck, fcd, cot)       # EN 1992-2 6.109(103): Eqs. 6.110 and 6.112
shell.principal_stresses(sx, sy, txy); shell.elastic_compression_angle(sx, sy, txy)
shell.deformation_capacity_ok_2004(1.0, 1.0, sx, sy, txy)  # 6.109(105) check of the reinforcement ductility

docs.title: Shell elements (sandwich model, both editions)
docs.text:
from eurocodepy.ec2 import uls, uls2023

inp = dict(n_xx=100, n_yy=50, n_xy=20, m_xx=20, m_yy=10, m_xy=5,      # kN/m and kNm/m
           fck=30, fyk=500, thickness=0.2, cover=0.04)
r = uls.eurocode2_shell_check(uls.ShellInput(**inp))                  # 2004: strut ≤ ν·fcd, ν = 0,6(1 − fck/250)
r23 = uls2023.eurocode2_shell_check(uls2023.ShellInput(**inp))        # 2023: Annex G.4, ν = 0,4 or G.9
r.asx_bot, r.asy_bot, r.asx_top, r.asy_top, r.crushing               # m²/m

Two layers of thickness t = 2·cover at z = h − t (EN 1992-2 Annex LL); each layer is a membrane (Table G.1 / Annex F); ftd·t/fyd gives the area and the strut of each layer is checked against ν·fcd. Sagging moments put the bottom layer in tension (EN 1992-2 Annex LL: the "top" layer of calc_reinf_shell is the upper one, +m/z).

Cracking (EN 1992-2 Annex LL (102)–(104), (107)): with check_cracking=True (default) the principal stresses of the uncracked section are evaluated through the thickness (shell_stresses_at_level) and the element is cracked where the Ottosen criterion (ottosen_phi, LL.101; fctm or Table 3.1) is exceeded. An element that is not cracked gets zero areas and only σmin ≤ fcd is checked: details["cracked"] is False. check_cracking=False designs it as cracked. shell_cracking(n, m, h, fck, v, f_ctm) returns the check on its own.

Out-of-plane shear: pass v_x, v_y (kN/m) to ShellInput (and to SlabInput in uls2023). The principal shear vEd0 = √(vx² + vy²) is verified as a beam of unit width — 2004: inner layer of Annex LL (109)–(111) with ρl = ρx·cos²φ0 + ρy·sin²φ0; 2023: clause 8.2 (G.4(4)). Where stirrups are needed (r.asw_s, m²/m²), the chord force vEd0·cot θ of the truss is added to the outer layers and the shell is redesigned; r.details["shear"] has the checks and a crushed shear strut sets r.crushing. check_shear=False skips it. uls.slab_check returns asw_s too, but the chord force is not added to the Wood-Armer bars.

docs.title: eurocodepy
docs.text:
Provide several functions to help designers working with Eurocodes.

The package provides modules for different Eurocodes and utilities, such as:

  • dbase: access to the database of materials, loads, sections, etc.
  • utils: utility functions for calculations, stress, and section properties.
  • ec1: utility functions for ec1 calculations.
  • ec2: utility functions for ec2 calculations.
  • ec3: utility functions for ec3 calculations.
  • ec5: utility functions for ec5 calculations.
  • ec7: utility functions for ec7 calculations.
  • ec8: utility functions for ec8 calculations.
Disclaimer

This library is intended for educational and research purposes only. It is not a certified engineering tool and must not be used for final structural designs. Always verify calculations against the official Eurocode standards and applicable national annexes, and have final designs reviewed and approved by a qualified structural engineer. The authors assume no liability for design decisions made using this library.
